title: Tensorized KV cache/view reconstruction
hypothesis: For a synthetic decoder with four layers and four KV heads, a shared temporal tensor basis plus compact layer/head Mirror coordinates will reconstruct aligned logical KV caches with held-out attention-output nMSE <= 1e-5 while reducing actual payload bytes by >=20% versus independent cache storage and remaining within 10% of the closest ordinary low-rank/MLKV control. Decode-time reconstruction operations and throughput must be reported.
physical_object: per-head temporal K/V cache tensors across four decoder layers, represented by shared rank-4 temporal bases over 128 token positions and 16 features
mirror_coordinate: small layer/head phase or coefficient codes applied during cache reconstruction
logical_multiplicity: sixteen layer/head KV cache views from shared physical cache factors
controls: independent full FP16 K/V cache per layer/head
MLKV-style hard shared cache across layers
shared temporal state with direct per-layer/head cos/sin coefficients plus private unrelated-layer cache
shared temporal state with Mirror phase codes plus private unrelated-layer cache
Mirror phase codes without private fallback for the deliberately unrelated layer

development.selection_metric: held-out attention-output nMSE, actual payload bytes, reconstruction MACs and eager CPU throughput

storage.authority: actual deterministic fixed-timestamp ZIP/NPY FP16 inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: All three fresh seeds: held-out attention-output nMSE <=1e-5; Mirror payload <=0.80x independent and <=1.10x closest ordinary shared-basis/MLKV control; reconstruction compute <=2x ordinary low-rank reconstruction; exact FP16 payload reload and metric replay.
failure_gate: At least two fresh seeds miss quality; or Mirror saves <20% bytes vs independent in at least two; or ordinary control is >10% smaller at comparable quality in at least two; or reconstruction compute exceeds 2x ordinary control.
amendment: Development source is frozen before fresh access. Canonical K/V states are stored as a rank-4 temporal basis with per-head coefficients. Decode timing is split into cache reconstruction wall time and causal attention wall time, and end-to-end query throughput includes both. Attention and reconstruction MAC proxies include both KQ and AV attention contractions and low-rank decode plus view rotations. Per-layer output nMSE is reported to expose private-state need. The quality and byte gates and fresh seeds are unchanged.
boundaries: synthetic attention-cache reconstruction, not natural language or trained nanoGPT evidence
logical cache multiplicity is not independent model capacity
report cache payload and decode-time reconstruction separately
no quality claim from cache-element error alone; attention outputs are primary
